questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Streaming pipelines must be validated for event-time correctness, late data handling, fault tolerance, and schema changes under production-like load. This question tests end-to-end thinking, data correctness guarantees, and practical testing strategies for a multi-region, high-volume system.

## Key Concepts

- Event-time vs. processing-time semantics
- Watermarks and late data handling
- Exactly-once delivery guarantees
- Backpressure and load testing
- Schema evolution and backward compatibility

## Code Example

```scala
import org.apache.spark.sql.SparkSession
import org.apache.spark.sql.functions._
import java.time.Instant

val spark = SparkSession.builder()
  .appName("WindowedAggregationTest")
  .getOrCreate()

import spark.implicits._

case class ClickEvent(
  userId: String,
  timestamp: Instant,
  region: String
)

val events = spark.readStream
  .format("kafka")
  .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092")
  .option("subscribe", "clickstream")
  .load()
  .select(from_json($"value".cast("string"), schema).as("data"))
  .select("data.*")
  .as[ClickEvent]

val windowedCounts = events
  .withWatermark("timestamp", "5 minutes")
  .groupBy(
    window($"timestamp", "1 minute"),
    $"region"
  )
  .agg(countDistinct("userId").as("unique_users"))

windowedCounts.writeStream
  .format("parquet")
  .option("checkpointLocation", "/tmp/checkpoints")
  .start("/output/path")
```
